notes: k29 'Rug' became Persian rug; its construction types (woven pile, tufted) and Wilton/Axminster go to the machine-made shelf, not here. Old Persian names became archetypes; Usak became the Ushak archetype and Kayseri stays an Anatolian model (no source detail); Baluchi moved to the Afghan & Baluch kind. Zanjan and Mehraban kept as plain models: no retrieved page describes them. Left out for lack of a retrieved source: Talish (Caucasian), Mahal (unless added), Amritsar and Lahore as separate archetypes (Lahore covered by Mughal carpet), Khal Mohammadi, Turkmen gul names (Turkmen_rug page names none), East Turkestan rugs. Versions limited to those stated on the source pages; no antique/new/reproduction split invented. Wikidata SPARQL was rate-limited.
